sources.title: Natural Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacking in Production RL
(Some) Natural Emergent Misalignment from Reward Hacking in Non-Production RL
sources.venue: UK AI Security Institute (Model Transparency Team), AI Alignment Forum, 30 March 2026; code at github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/reward-hacking-misalignment

extracted: MacDiarmid et al. (2025), Figure 9 (appendix table of misalignment rates, Section 3), read from the arXiv HTML render of v1; caption of Figure 2 for the sabotage rate quoted in notes; Section 4.1 and Figure 6 for the RLHF result described qualitatively in notes
notes: Every number is the rate reported in the table of Figure 9 of MacDiarmid et al. (2025), averaged across the final five RL checkpoints, with the standard error over checkpoint means given in the paper after the value (SDF hacking: 33.7+/-0.4, 69.8+/-1.2, 39.9+/-1.2, 31.8+/-3.5, 1.6+/-0.2, 41.3+/-1.8; SDF baseline: 0.7+/-0.3, 0.1+/-0.1, 0.3+/-0.1, 0.2+/-0.2, 0.0+/-0.0, 4.0+/-0.2; prompted hacking: 4.8+/-0.6, 17.1+/-1.3, 9.0+/-0.2, 24.6+/-2.4, 0.4+/-0.1, 37.4+/-1.6; prompted baseline: 0.3+/-0.2, 1.5+/-0.3, 0.2+/-0.1, 1.2+/-0.4, 0.0+/-0.0, 3.5+/-0.7). The baseline is an RL run on the same coding environments in which reward hacking was disincentivised with a reward-hacking penalty, not an untrained model; the paper states that production Claude Sonnet 3.7 and Claude Sonnet 4 score zero on all these evaluations. The first three evaluations are chat-like, the last three are agentic. The models are research models, not deployed ones, and the synthetic document finetuning step exists only to teach the reward hacks; the paper reports (Figure 9) that SDF alone does not raise initial misalignment. Separately, in the Claude Code sabotage evaluation the paper reports attempted sabotage in 12% of episodes for the main SDF hacking model, with the sabotaged classifiers only 65% as effective as a baseline (Figure 2 caption). The UK AI Security Institute reproduction on open-source models (OLMo 7B/32B, GPT-OSS 20B/120B) found consistent reward hacking during RL but inconsistent and lower emergent misalignment across evaluations, so the size of the generalization effect should not be treated as settled.
